disagreements.topic: Exit multiple: 16x vs 16.5x FY28 core EPS
disagreements.positions: Agents 1 and 4: 16.5x, because Flex trades at ~25x and Jabil is committing new capacity for FY28. Agents 2, 3 and 5: 16x, because working capital is funded by payables and the 2028 capex slowdown will be priced by the horizon.
disagreements.resolution: Not settled by evidence, and it matters little: 0.5x is about $10/share, or roughly 0.01-0.02 of probability per strike near the money. Both sides rest on verified facts: Flex ~25x (round 1), the +$8B payables funding (8-K), and the UBS 2028 capex path (verified below). The mean already sits between the two camps, so I leave it there.

disagreements.positions: Agent 3 stays at $20.0, citing UBS's view that hyperscaler capex grows only +6% in 2028, the year that overlaps Jabil's FY28. The others use $20.4-20.6 built from the segment guide, buybacks and the beat record.
disagreements.resolution: The UBS figure is real and quoted correctly: capex +76% in 2026 to $673B, +25% in 2027, +6% in 2028. It is one bank's forecast, though, and Morgan Stanley (+29% in 2027) and Goldman (~$1.14T in 2027, consensus too low) are more bullish for 2027. Jabil's FY28 runs Sep-2027 to Aug-2028, so only about two-thirds of it overlaps 2028 capex. The +6% supports agent 3's thinner upper tail, which matters at the September 2027 FY28 guide, but it does not establish a lower centre. The spread is $0.6 of EPS, about $10/share.
disagreements.evidence: EMSNow reprint of Reuters, 2026-07-20 (fetched): 'UBS estimating hyperscalers' capex will rise 76% this year to $673 billion, but will increase by only 25% next year and just 6% in 2028.'

disagreements.positions: Agent 3: 0.15 / 0.072 / 0.03 / 0.006. Agents 1 and 2: 0.19 / 0.10 / 0.055 / 0.016. Agent 5 keeps 0.095 at 533, arguing that it needs a peer multiple JBL has never held.
disagreements.resolution: The base rates are verified: since 2000, 9 of 26 Sep-to-Sep years returned more than 30% and 4 of 26 more than 50%, but most of those came off depressed multiples (2009-10, 2023-24), not off a 17x forward P/E after a 3-year run-up. Reaching 533 (+75%) needs about $22.5 EPS at about 24x. The mean (0.091 at 533) sits between the camps, and I have no evidence to move it.
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data monthly closes for JBL, 2000-2026, recomputed by me: median +6.3% price-only, 54% of years up, log SD 0.41, 3 of 26 years down 20% or more, 2 of 26 down more than 30%.

disagreements.topic: Size of the FY24 guide miss (base rate for a guide cut)
disagreements.positions: Agent 1: initial ~$33.3B midpoint and '>$9.00', later cut to $28.5B / $8.40. Agent 5: an initial EPS of ~$9.45, from memory, implying a ~10% miss.
disagreements.resolution: Partly settled. The Dec-2023 8-K confirms the amended FY24 outlook of $31B and $9.00+ core EPS, and the Nov-2023 release says $31B was 7% below the prior revenue midpoint (about $33.3B). FY24 actual core EPS was $8.49. The initial Sept-2023 EPS figure was not retrieved, so the miss is somewhere between -6% and -10%. Either way the base rate is 2 big beats, 1 small beat and 1 miss over FY22-26, as agent 5 says, and every agent already weights it.

disagreements.topic: New capacity as evidence of FY28 demand (agent 4)
disagreements.positions: Agent 4 cites a second Marshall County, MS site (1.5M sq ft, ~$119M, ~2,200 jobs) as support for 16.5x. The others do not mention it.
disagreements.resolution: Verified: announced 2026-07-11 for data-center infrastructure equipment, an existing facility being renovated, with no start date given. It shows Jabil is committing capacity but carries no volume or customer data, and it adds fixed-cost risk if 2028 capex slows. Direction-neutral for the ladder.

disagreements.positions: Agents agree that no Jabil print falls in the window. Agent 2 dates Celestica to 2026-10-26, agent 5 dates the FOMC to 2026-10-28, and agent 4 lists the US midterms on 2026-11-03.
disagreements.resolution: The FOMC decision on 2026-10-28 is confirmed. Celestica's 10-26 date is an Earnings Whispers estimate, not yet confirmed by the company (it reported Q3 2025 on 10-27). The midterms on 11-03 fall after the 11-01 horizon and are out of the window. The 1m ladders differ by at most 0.02 at any strike, so I keep the mean.
disagreements.evidence: federalreserve.gov October 2026 calendar via search; Celestica IR via search.

one_month_reasoning: No Jabil print falls before 2026-11-01. The window holds the FY26 10-K (late October), hyperscaler Q3 capex calls and the Celestica/Flex prints (late October; Celestica's ~10-26 date is unconfirmed), and the FOMC on 10-28. The midterms (11-03) fall after the window. The five forecasters agree within 0.02 at every strike on a near-symmetric ~13.5% monthly sigma with a slight upward tilt after the 10% sell-off partly retraced; I keep their mean.
confidence_reason: Round 2 converged: fair values are $317-335 and the 12-month ladders sit within 0.02-0.04 of each other except in agent 3's upper tail. My checks confirmed the new claims (UBS 2027/2028 capex path, Marshall County site, agent 5's 26-year base rates, the FOMC date). None settled a disagreement in a way that moves the distribution, so I leave the ladder at the forecasters' mean and make no update.
thesis_break_reason: $211 is 12x the confirmed $17.55 FY27 core EPS guide (the pre-AI EMS multiple) and about 31% below spot. It is well under the $284-287 lows that held through the July-September 2026 AI-hardware sell-off and the post-print drop. A close there would price a guide cut like FY24's or a flat FY28 (a hyperscaler pause, consignment shift or capex digestion as UBS's +6% 2028 path arrives) together with a payables unwind. The forecasters cluster at $205-215, with a mean of $211.
key_drivers: FY27 guide (8-K, 2026-09-30): $44.5B revenue (+24%), 6.1% core margin, $17.55 core EPS, ~$1.6B adj FCF, ~3.7% above the $16.92 consensus. The stock is at 17.3x it vs Flex at ~25x.

AI concentration: $22.1B of AI revenue (+54%), about half the guide, with cloud/data center $17.5B (+52%). UBS sees hyperscaler capex growth at +25% in 2027 and +6% in 2028, so the late-Sept 2027 FY28 guide arrives as the market prices a slowdown.

Guide record over FY22-26: beats of about +20%, +1%, +13% and +19%, and one miss (FY24, -6% to -10%). Even after the miss year the stock fell only ~6%. Buybacks shrink shares ~3% a year, supporting FY28 core EPS of ~$20.0-20.6.

Earnings quality: FCF is flat at ~$1.6B on +24% revenue, FY26 working capital was funded by +$8B of payables (AP $14.4B vs equity $1.6B), and GAAP EPS is 26% below core. This keeps the multiple at 16-16.5x rather than at the peer level.
Base rates (26 Sep-Sep years since 2000): median +6%, 54% of years up, log SD 0.41. Both crashes of more than 50% followed multi-year run-ups and end-market busts, which is the setup to watch.

fair_value.reason: Forecasters now span $317-335 (mean $327.6) on near-identical inputs: FY28 core EPS of $20.0-20.6 at 16-16.5x ($320-340), and FY28 adj FCF of $1.75-1.85B on ~100-102M diluted shares at a 5.25-5.75% yield ($312-334). Net debt is $1.64B. No input remains in factual error. I take ~$20.4 x 16.25x = ~$331 for P/E and ~$324 for FCF yield, which blends to ~$327, about 7% above spot. This is essentially the mean.

summary: The five forecasters converged in round 2: fair values of $317-335 (mean ~$327, ~7% above spot), FY28 core EPS of $20.0-20.6 at 16-16.5x, a fat left tail (~17% below $213) and a thesis break near $211 (12x the $17.55 guide). My checks confirmed the new evidence: UBS sees hyperscaler capex growth at +25% in 2027 and +6% in 2028, Jabil has a second Mississippi data-center site, and JBL's 26-year Sep-to-Sep record shows a median of +6% with a log SD of 0.41. None of it moves the distribution, so I keep the forecasters' mean ladder. The risk to watch is the late-Sept 2027 FY28 guide landing just as the market prices the 2028 capex slowdown, on a model whose growth is funded by payables.
